div.div:
1 حَنَطَ , (K,) aor.
حَنُطَ , (TK,) inf. n. حُنُوطٌ, It (seed-produce) attained to the time for its being reaped; as also ↓ احنط . (K.) ―
-b2- It (a tree of the kind called رِمْث) became mature, and its leaves became white; as also ↓ احنط : (S:) or it became white and mature, (K, TA,) and there came forth upon it a dust-coloured fruit, and what resembled pieces of glue appeared upon its tops; (TA;) as also حَنِطَ, aor.
حَنَطَ ; (K, TA;) and ↓ احنط : (TA:) [the last, though omitted in the K, seems to be the most common:] or its colour became white inclining to yellowness, and its odour sweet: (IAth:) Az relates, on the authority of IAar, that one says, أَوْرَسَ الرِّمْثُ, and ↓ احنط ; like خَضَبَ العَرْفَجُ: and one says, of the رِمْث, when it first breaks out for its leaves to come forth, قَدْ أَقْمَلَ; and when it has increased little by little, قَدْ أَدْبَى; and when its greenness has increased, بَقَلَ: and when it has become white and mature, حَنَطَ: (TA:) or ↓ احنط is said of a tree, and of a herb, meaning its fruit became mature; and so حَنَطَ, inf. n. حُنُوطٌ. (AHn.) ―
-b3- It (leather) became red. (S, K.) [The inf. n. of the verb in this sense is not mentioned.] ＝
-A2- See also 2.
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
